# TideSurf

> Stateful Chromium tools for agents. TideSurf compresses the live DOM into compact text and assigns action IDs to current elements.

Package: @tidesurf/core
CLI: tidesurf
Runtime: Node.js 18+ or Bun 1+
Docs: https://tidesurf.org/docs
Source: https://github.com/TideSurf/core

## Agent CLI

The first tool command starts a private local daemon and a managed headless browser. Separate CLI invocations reuse the same browser, active tab, open tabs, and element ID maps. The default session name is `default`.

```sh
tidesurf navigate https://example.com
tidesurf get-state
tidesurf click B1
tidesurf stop
```

Use `--session <name>` on every command for an independent workflow:

```sh
tidesurf --session docs navigate https://example.com/docs
tidesurf --session docs get-state --max-tokens 800
```

Session commands:

- `start`: start the session daemon and browser
- `status`: report session and browser state without starting either
- `stop`: stop the named session; repeated calls succeed
- `tools`: list the shared tool registry
- `help [command]`: show generated help
- `call <tool> --input <json|->`: call a canonical name or CLI alias with JSON; `-` reads stdin
- `inspect <url>`: one-shot compatibility command
- `mcp`: run the MCP stdio adapter

Direct tool commands, in registry order:

1. `get-state` (`get_state`)
2. `navigate`
3. `click`
4. `type`
5. `select`
6. `scroll`
7. `extract`
8. `evaluate`
9. `list-tabs` (`list_tabs`)
10. `new-tab` (`new_tab`)
11. `switch-tab` (`switch_tab`)
12. `close-tab` (`close_tab`)
13. `search`
14. `screenshot`
15. `upload`
16. `clipboard-read` (`clipboard_read`)
17. `clipboard-write` (`clipboard_write`)
18. `download`

Use `tidesurf help <command>` for exact positionals and flags. Page-state flags:

- `get-state --max-tokens <n> --mode <full|minimal|interactive>`
- `get-state --full-page` disables normal viewport filtering
- `get-state --include-hidden` includes hidden nodes and disables viewport filtering
- `screenshot --element-id <id> | --full-page`
- `screenshot --output <file>` writes a selected file
- `screenshot --output -` writes raw PNG bytes to stdout

Without `--output`, screenshot writes a unique temporary PNG and prints its absolute path.

Default output is readable text or pretty JSON. `--json` returns the ToolResult shape:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": "..." }
```

Exit codes: 0 Success; 2 CLI usage or input parsing error; 3 Session or browser startup/connection error; 4 Tool execution failed; 5 Daemon authentication, transport, or protocol error.

## Browser startup

Managed isolated Chromium is the default. Launch is headless unless `--headful` is set. TideSurf selects an ephemeral debugging port unless `--port` is explicit.

Browser resolution order:

1. `--chrome-path`
2. `CHROME_PATH`
3. executable on `PATH`
4. platform install locations, including macOS user applications and Windows LOCALAPPDATA

Channel order: stable, Beta, Dev, Canary, Chromium. Select one with `--channel stable|beta|dev|canary|chromium`. Edge and Brave need `--chrome-path`. TideSurf never downloads a browser.

`--auto-connect` tries an explicit endpoint, a current Chrome profile DevToolsActivePort entry, then a conventional local CDP endpoint before local launch. `--connect-only` never launches. Failure on a remote host never starts a local browser.

Startup and policy flags:

`--headful`, `--auto-connect`, `--connect-only`, `--browser-url`, `--host`, `--port`, `--chrome-path`, `--channel`, `--user-data-dir`, `--read-only`, `--allow-localhost`, `--allow-private-hosts`, repeatable `--file-access-root`, `--timeout`.

For `download`, `--timeout` after the command sets the download wait. Put the global `--timeout` before `download` to set the session operation timeout.

Session policy is immutable. Later calls may omit startup flags or repeat matching standalone values. Browser-mode flag combinations must resolve to the stored mode, and a repeated `--file-access-root` set must match the complete stored list. Conflicting explicit values require `stop` or another session name. Sessions have no idle shutdown.

## Page format

```text
# Example Search
> example.com/search | 0/1200 800vh

NAV
  [L1](/) Home
FORM F1
  I1 ~Search... ="TideSurf"
  [B1] Search
```

Prefixes: L link, B button, I input, S select, F form, T table, D dialog.

IDs refer to the in-memory state map. Read new state after navigation or a dynamic page update. Never guess a replacement ID after a stale-ID error.

Default state uses viewport filtering. `includeHidden: true` is a full-DOM debugging override, not only a CSS-hidden override.

## SDK

```ts
import { TideSurf } from "@tidesurf/core";

const browser = await TideSurf.launch();
await browser.navigate("https://example.com");
const state = await browser.getState({ maxTokens: 1000 });
await browser.getPage().click("B1");
await browser.close();
```

`TideSurf.launch(options)` strictly launches and owns Chrome. An unspecified launch port is ephemeral. `TideSurf.connect(options)` strictly attaches and defaults to `localhost:9222`. Closing an attached instance only disconnects.

`TideSurfOptions.channel` accepts `stable`, `beta`, `dev`, `canary`, or `chromium`.

The package-level `getToolDefinitions()` and a normal instance return all 18 schemas used by the CLI and MCP. A read-only instance or `getToolDefinitions({ readOnly: true })` returns the six observation schemas. `getToolExecutor()` accepts `{ name, input }` and returns ToolResult.

## Read-only mode

Allowed tools: `get_state`, `extract`, `list_tabs`, `switch_tab`, `search`, `screenshot`.

Blocked operations: navigation, interaction, evaluation, clipboard, upload/download, tab creation, tab closure. Enforcement applies in the registry, executor, MCP adapter, TideSurf methods, and SurfingPage returned by `getPage()`.

## Evaluate

`evaluate` runs arbitrary JavaScript in the page. TideSurf validates input shape and size; it does not provide a JavaScript sandbox. CDP values such as `NaN`, infinity, negative zero, and bigint return as JSON-safe strings. Read-only mode removes and rejects the tool.

## Files and URLs

SDK uploads and downloads stay inside `fileAccessRoots`. Omit the option for the working directory and OS temporary directory; pass `fileAccessRoots: []` to disable SDK filesystem operations. The CLI adds roots with repeatable `--file-access-root` flags.

Localhost, loopback, private, and link-local navigation is blocked by default. Use `allowLocalhost` or `allowPrivateHosts` only for trusted targets.

## MCP

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tidesurf": {
      "command": "bunx",
      "args": ["@tidesurf/core", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

The MCP adapter registers the shared 18 tools and the compatibility-only `launch_browser` tool. Screenshot results become image blocks. Failed tool calls set `isError`. `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `zod` are optional package dependencies.
